notes: Religious & occult symbol library for Hathor Studio and the Hierophant. Each symbol has a 512px black-on-transparent PNG (<id>.png), a coloured original where meaningful (<id>.orig.png) and, for Commons SVGs, the source vector in src/. Images: Wikimedia Commons files kept ONLY if Public Domain / CC0 / CC BY / CC BY-SA (bucket A = PD/CC0, bucket B = attribution/share-alike required — credit `author` and link `source`), or Unicode characters rendered from Noto fonts (SIL OFL). `sources` are the Wikipedia articles the harvester fetched for that symbol. `figures` are ids in integrations/hierophant-entities.mjs, pantheon-map.mjs or divine-attributes.mjs. `status`: attested | disputed | modern — read `note` before presenting a modern or disputed symbol as ancient. Built by integrations/genai-symbol-harvest.mjs + integrations/symbol_library.py from integrations/symbol-library-spec.mjs.

symbols.name: Ankh
symbols.meaning: Hieroglyph for "life" (ꜥnḫ). Gods hold it by the loop and offer it to the king's nose as the breath of life; it survives as the Coptic crux ansata.
symbols.note: Meaning is attested; the object the shape originally depicted (sandal strap, knot, etc.) is disputed.

image.author: No machine-readable author provided. AmosWolfe assumed (based on copyright claims).
image.title: File:Ankh.svg

symbols.name: Djed pillar
symbols.meaning: Pillar sign for "stability"; linked to Ptah and, from the New Kingdom, read as the backbone of Osiris. Raised in the "Raising of the Djed" rite.

symbols.name: Was-sceptre
symbols.meaning: Straight staff with a forked foot and an animal head (often the Set-animal) — "power, dominion", carried by gods and kings.

symbols.name: Eye of Horus (wedjat)
symbols.period: Old Kingdom (c. 2600 BCE); amulets from late Old Kingdom
symbols.meaning: The eye of Horus torn out by Set and restored (by Thoth or Hathor) — wholeness, healing, protection and royal power; one of the most common amulets.
symbols.note: The popular reading of its parts as the "Horus-eye fractions" (1/2 … 1/64) is disputed in modern Egyptology.

symbols.name: Eye of Ra
symbols.meaning: The sun's eye as a feminine, sometimes violent force acting for Ra — embodied by Hathor, Sekhmet, Bastet and Wadjet (the uraeus).
symbols.note: Graphically usually indistinguishable from the wedjat; the "left eye = Horus / right eye = Ra" rule is a modern simplification.

symbols.name: Scarab (kheper)
symbols.period: Old Kingdom; amulets and seals from First Intermediate Period
symbols.meaning: The dung-beetle as Khepri rolling the sun into being each dawn — "becoming" (ḫpr), renewal; heart-scarabs guarded the heart at judgment.

symbols.name: Shen ring
symbols.meaning: A loop of rope tied at the base — eternity and encircling protection; stretched out it becomes the cartouche around a royal name.

symbols.name: Tyet (Knot of Isis)
symbols.period: Old Kingdom; funerary amulet (Book of the Dead ch. 156) New Kingdom
symbols.meaning: A knotted cloth resembling an ankh with drooping arms — "welfare/life", the "blood of Isis" amulet of red stone placed on the mummy.

symbols.name: Sistrum
symbols.period: Old Kingdom (naos-sistrum); later Isis cult across the Roman world
symbols.meaning: Sacred rattle of Hathor — shaken to pacify the goddess and drive off evil; the handle often bears Hathor's cow-eared face.

symbols.name: Uraeus
symbols.meaning: The rearing cobra on the royal brow — the goddess Wadjet, spitting fire at the king's enemies; sovereignty and divine protection.

symbols.name: Winged sun disk (Behdety)
symbols.period: Old Kingdom; over temple gateways from Middle Kingdom
symbols.meaning: Horus of Behdet as a sun disk with outstretched falcon wings and two uraei — protection over the doorway and the king.

symbols.name: Crook and flail
symbols.meaning: The heqa crook and nekhakha flail — insignia of kingship, held crossed by Osiris and the pharaoh.

symbols.name: Feather of Maʿat
symbols.period: Old Kingdom; judgment scene New Kingdom
symbols.meaning: The ostrich feather of Maʿat — truth and cosmic order, weighed against the heart of the dead in the Hall of Two Truths.

symbols.name: Menat
symbols.meaning: A heavy beaded necklace with a counterpoise, shaken like the sistrum in Hathor's rites — fertility, rebirth, the goddess's favour.

symbols.name: Akhet (horizon)
symbols.meaning: Hieroglyph of the sun rising between two mountains — the horizon, place of daily rebirth, guarded by the lion-god Aker.

symbols.name: Cow horns and sun disk
symbols.period: Old Kingdom; adopted by Isis in the New Kingdom
symbols.meaning: Hathor's headdress — the solar disk cradled in lyre-shaped cow horns, often with a uraeus; later worn by Isis.

symbols.name: Sema-tawy
symbols.meaning: "Union of the Two Lands": lotus (Upper Egypt) and papyrus (Lower Egypt) tied around the lung-and-windpipe sign, often by Horus and Set or two Hapi figures.

symbols.name: Ka (raised arms)
symbols.meaning: Two upraised arms — the ka, the vital double that receives offerings and survives death.

sources.title: Ancient Egyptian conception of the soul

symbols.name: Star of Ishtar
symbols.period: Early Dynastic / Old Akkadian (3rd millennium BCE); prominent on Kassite kudurrus
symbols.meaning: Eight-pointed star of Inanna/Ishtar, the planet Venus — love, war and the morning/evening star.

symbols.name: Assyrian winged disc
symbols.meaning: Winged disc, often with a god in a ring — divine presence and protection over the king; borrowed from Egypt via the Levant.
symbols.note: Whether the figure-in-disc is Ashur or Shamash is debated.

symbols.name: Lamassu
symbols.meaning: Human-headed winged bull or lion flanking palace gates — protective genius guarding the threshold.

symbols.name: Sun disk of Shamash
symbols.meaning: Disk with a four-pointed star and wavy rays — Utu/Shamash, sun-god of justice (as on the Code of Hammurabi stele and kudurrus).

symbols.name: Crescent of Sin
symbols.meaning: The crescent moon of Nanna/Sin, moon-god of Ur and Harran.

symbols.name: Dingir (god sign)
symbols.meaning: Cuneiform AN / DINGIR — "sky" and the determinative written before a god's name.

symbols.name: Assyrian sacred tree
symbols.meaning: Stylised tree of palmettes flanked by genii with cone and bucket — divine abundance and royal order.
symbols.note: Its meaning is contested; Parpola's reading as a proto-Kabbalistic Tree of Life is controversial.

symbols.name: Rod and ring
symbols.period: Ur III (Ur-Nammu stele, c. 2100 BCE); Code of Hammurabi
symbols.meaning: The rod and ring handed by a god to the king — kingship and justice.
symbols.note: Identified variously as measuring rod and line, or a halter and nose-rope; not settled.

symbols.name: Spade of Marduk (marru)
symbols.meaning: The triangular-bladed spade — emblem of Marduk on boundary stones.

symbols.name: Mušḫuššu
symbols.meaning: The scaly serpent-dragon with lion forelegs and eagle hind legs — beast of Marduk (earlier of Ninazu and Tishpak).

symbols.name: Sign of Tanit
symbols.period: Punic, from c. 5th c. BCE (Carthage Tophet stelae)
symbols.meaning: Triangle (or trapezoid) with a horizontal bar and a disc — the goddess Tanit, "face of Baal", on thousands of Carthaginian votive stelae.
symbols.note: Its origin (a stylised woman, a derivation from the ankh, an altar) is debated.

symbols.name: Crescent and disc
symbols.period: Phoenician and Punic stelae (1st millennium BCE)
symbols.meaning: A disc resting above a down-turned crescent — the heavenly pair, associated with Baal Hammon and Tanit.

symbols.name: Caduceus
symbols.period: Archaic Greek (vases from 6th c. BCE); Mesopotamian antecedents
symbols.meaning: Herald's staff entwined by two snakes, often winged — Hermes/Mercury: heralds, commerce, safe passage, guide of souls.
symbols.note: Its use as a medical emblem (US Army Medical Corps, 1902) is a modern confusion with the rod of Asclepius.

symbols.name: Rod of Asclepius
symbols.meaning: A single serpent on a rough staff — healing and medicine, the god Asklepios.

symbols.name: Labrys
symbols.period: Minoan Crete (c. 2000–1450 BCE); Carian Zeus Labraundos
symbols.meaning: The double-headed axe — a central Minoan cult object; later the weapon of Zeus Labraundos.
symbols.note: The derivation of "labyrinth" from labrys is disputed. Modern uses (Hellenic polytheism, lesbian-feminist emblem) are 20th-century.

symbols.name: Thyrsus
symbols.meaning: Fennel staff tipped with a pine cone and wound with ivy — carried by Dionysos, satyrs and maenads; fertility and ecstatic release.

symbols.name: Owl of Athena
symbols.meaning: The little owl (Athene noctua) — wisdom and the city of Athens; the goddess's companion.

symbols.name: Thunderbolt (keraunos)
symbols.meaning: Zeus's thunderbolt, forged by the Cyclopes — sovereign power and divine judgment.

symbols.name: Trident of Poseidon
symbols.meaning: Three-pronged fishing spear of Poseidon/Neptune — mastery of sea, earthquakes and horses.

symbols.name: Gorgoneion
symbols.meaning: The Gorgon's head on Athena's aegis and on shields and antefixes — apotropaic, turning evil away.

symbols.name: Omphalos
symbols.meaning: The "navel" stone of Delphi marking the centre of the world, where Zeus's two eagles met; Apollo's oracle.

symbols.name: Lyre of Apollo
symbols.meaning: Tortoise-shell lyre invented by Hermes and given to Apollo — music, harmony, order.

image.author: Alexey Gomankov based on Urbi et orbi
image.title: File:Lyre.svg

symbols.name: Trinacria (triskeles of Sicily)
symbols.period: Greek coinage of Syracuse (4th c. BCE)
symbols.meaning: Three bent legs radiating from a Gorgon head — Sicily, the "three-cornered" island.

symbols.name: Hekate's wheel (strophalos)
symbols.period: Chaldean Oracles (2nd c. CE) — the ritual top; the maze-wheel design is 20th-c.
symbols.meaning: The strophalos/iynx of Hekate spun in theurgic rites. The labyrinthine wheel sold today under this name is a modern Wiccan design.
symbols.note: The strophalos is ancient; the popular "Hecate's wheel" graphic is a modern (20th-c. Wiccan/Dianic) design.

symbols.name: Cornucopia
symbols.meaning: Horn of plenty — the horn of the goat Amalthea; abundance, carried by Demeter, Tyche/Fortuna and Plutus.

symbols.name: Tetractys
symbols.meaning: Ten points in a triangle of 1-2-3-4 — the Pythagorean oath-figure of cosmic harmony.

symbols.name: Star of David (Magen David)
symbols.period: Decorative in antiquity; Jewish emblem from medieval Prague (1354); general symbol 17th–19th c.
symbols.meaning: Hexagram — the emblem of Judaism and the Jewish people; on the Zionist flag (1897) and Israel's flag.
symbols.note: The hexagram is ancient and pan-cultural; its use as THE symbol of Judaism is medieval-to-modern (not biblical).

symbols.name: Menorah
symbols.period: Exodus 25 (Tabernacle); Second Temple; Arch of Titus (81 CE)
symbols.meaning: Seven-branched lampstand of the Tabernacle and Temple — the oldest Jewish emblem; the state emblem of Israel.

symbols.name: Tree of Life (Kabbalah)
symbols.period: Sefirot from the Bahir/Zohar (12th–13th c.); diagram from 16th c. (Portae Lucis 1516; Kircher 1652)
symbols.meaning: The ten sefirot and twenty-two paths — the emanation of Ein Sof into the world; map of the soul's ascent.

symbols.name: Hamsa
symbols.period: Attested in North Africa and the Middle East; widespread from the medieval period
symbols.meaning: Open palm amulet against the evil eye — "Hand of Fatima" (Muslim), "Hand of Miriam" (Jewish), found across the Maghreb and Levant.
symbols.note: A pre-Islamic (Punic / Tanit) origin is often claimed but not established; "Hand of Miriam" is a modern name.

symbols.name: Tablets of the Law
symbols.period: Exodus 31–34; round-topped form from medieval Christian art
symbols.meaning: The two stone tablets of the Ten Commandments given to Moses at Sinai — covenant and Torah.

symbols.name: Chai (חי)
symbols.period: Medieval Spain (use as emblem); common from 18th c.
symbols.meaning: The Hebrew word "alive" (ḥet-yod), numerically 18 — life; worn as an amulet.
symbols.note: Word is ancient; its use as a standalone emblem is medieval-to-modern.

symbols.name: Tetragrammaton (יהוה)
symbols.period: Mesha Stele (c. 840 BCE) — earliest extra-biblical attestation
symbols.meaning: The four-letter name YHWH — the ineffable Name of the God of Israel; central in Kabbalah and Christian-Hermetic magic.

symbols.name: Latin cross
symbols.meaning: The cross of the crucifixion — the principal Christian symbol.

symbols.name: Orthodox cross
symbols.meaning: Three-bar cross: the titulus above, the slanted footrest below (pointing up to the repentant thief).

symbols.name: Cross of Lorraine
symbols.period: Byzantine patriarchal cross; Anjou/Lorraine from 15th c.
symbols.meaning: Two-barred cross; heraldic cross of the Dukes of Lorraine, emblem of Free France (1940).

symbols.name: Jerusalem cross
symbols.meaning: A cross potent with four small crosses — the five wounds, or Christ and the four evangelists; arms of the Crusader kingdom.

symbols.name: Maltese cross
symbols.meaning: Eight-pointed cross — the eight beatitudes; emblem of the Order of St John.

symbols.name: Celtic cross
symbols.period: Early medieval Ireland and Britain (8th–9th c. high crosses)
symbols.meaning: Latin cross with a ring around the intersection — Insular Christianity.
symbols.note: Folk explanations (a Christianised sun-cross, St Patrick) are legends; the ring's origin is uncertain.

symbols.name: Coptic cross (crux ansata)
symbols.meaning: The ankh taken up by Egyptian Christians as the cross of life; later the equal-armed Coptic cross with circle.

symbols.name: Tau cross
symbols.meaning: T-shaped cross of St Anthony and St Francis — from Ezekiel 9:4, the mark on the foreheads of the faithful.

symbols.name: Papal cross
symbols.meaning: Three-barred cross — the papal office.

symbols.name: Cross of St Peter (inverted cross)
symbols.period: Early medieval, from the tradition of Peter's inverted crucifixion
symbols.meaning: Upside-down Latin cross — humility of St Peter; a papal symbol.
symbols.note: Its reading as an anti-Christian sign is modern (20th-c. popular culture).

symbols.name: Saltire (St Andrew's cross)
symbols.period: Medieval (10th–14th c. legend of Andrew's X-shaped cross)
symbols.meaning: X-shaped cross of St Andrew; flag of Scotland.

symbols.name: Chi-Rho
symbols.meaning: ΧΡ, the first two letters of Christos — Constantine's labarum and the imperial Christian monogram.

symbols.name: Staurogram
symbols.period: Early Christian papyri (c. 200 CE, P66, P75)
symbols.meaning: Tau-Rho ligature ⳨ — a pictogram of Christ on the cross, among the earliest Christian images.

image.author: F l a n k e r
image.title: File:Staurogram.svg

symbols.name: Ichthys
symbols.meaning: Fish; ΙΧΘΥΣ = "Jesus Christ, God's Son, Saviour" — a recognition sign of early Christians.

symbols.name: Alpha and Omega
symbols.meaning: First and last letters of the Greek alphabet — God and Christ as beginning and end.

image.author: Trlkly
image.title: File:Uppercase Alpha and Omega in Times New Roman.svg

symbols.name: IHS Christogram
symbols.meaning: Abbreviation of ΙΗΣΟΥΣ — the Holy Name of Jesus.

symbols.name: Agnus Dei
symbols.meaning: The Lamb of God with a cross-banner — Christ's sacrifice and victory.

image.author: Hstoops
image.title: File:Lamb of God Saint John (agnus dei).svg

symbols.name: Sacred Heart
symbols.meaning: Flaming heart ringed by thorns and topped by a cross — Christ's love.
symbols.note: Devotion has medieval roots; the standard emblem is 17th-century.

symbols.name: Shield of the Trinity
symbols.meaning: Scutum Fidei: diagram of the three Persons, each "is God" and "is not" the others.

image.author: User:AnonMoos (earlier version of SVG file Sumudu Fernando)
image.title: File:Shield-Trinity-Scutum-Fidei-English.svg

symbols.name: Star and crescent
symbols.period: Ancient Near East & Byzantium; Ottoman state emblem late 18th c.; "Islamic" symbol 20th c.
symbols.meaning: Crescent with a star — adopted from Ottoman flags as a general emblem of Islam in the 20th century.
symbols.note: NOT scriptural — neither the Qur'an nor the Prophet used it; many Muslims reject it as a religious symbol.

symbols.name: Rubʿ el Hizb
symbols.meaning: Eight-pointed star of two overlapping squares ۞ — marks quarters of a hizb in the Qur'an.

symbols.name: Allah (calligraphy)
symbols.meaning: The name of God (ﷲ) written as a calligraphic ligature.

image.author: The original uploader was Mr100percent at Wikipedia.
image.title: File:Allah-green.svg

symbols.name: Zulfiqar
symbols.meaning: The forked sword of ʿAli — emblem of Shiʿi Islam and of courage.

symbols.name: Om (Aum)
symbols.period: Upanishads (1st millennium BCE); the ॐ ligature is medieval
symbols.meaning: The primordial sacred syllable — Brahman in sound; chanted at the start of recitations (Mandukya Upanishad).

symbols.name: Trishula
symbols.period: Kushan-era coins (1st–3rd c. CE); Shaiva iconography
symbols.meaning: Trident of Shiva (and Durga) — the three gunas, or creation, preservation and destruction.

symbols.name: Sri Yantra
symbols.meaning: Nine interlocking triangles around the bindu — the goddess Tripura Sundari and the union of Shiva and Shakti.

symbols.name: Swastika (Hindu / Buddhist / Jain)
symbols.period: Neolithic; Indus Valley seals (c. 2500 BCE); Vedic "svasti"
symbols.meaning: From Sanskrit svasti, "well-being" — auspiciousness, the sun, Ganesha; in Jainism the four states of existence.
symbols.note: Pan-Eurasian and ancient. The Nazi Hakenkreuz (1920, rotated 45°) is a 20th-c. appropriation unrelated to its Dharmic meaning.

symbols.name: Lingam
symbols.meaning: The aniconic form of Shiva, usually set in the yoni — creation, the union of Shiva and Shakti.

symbols.name: Lotus (padma)
symbols.meaning: Purity rising unstained from the mud — seat of Lakshmi, Brahma and the Buddha; one of the Eight Auspicious Signs.

symbols.name: Shankha (conch)
symbols.meaning: Right-turning conch — Vishnu's Panchajanya; the sound of the Dharma; one of the Eight Auspicious Signs.

image.author: This image has been extracted from another file
image.title: File:Simple conch shell.svg

symbols.name: Sudarshana Chakra
symbols.meaning: The spinning discus of Vishnu and Krishna — cosmic order cutting through evil.

symbols.name: Damaru
symbols.meaning: Hourglass drum of Shiva — the rhythm of creation from which sound and grammar arose.

symbols.name: Vel
symbols.meaning: The divine spear of Murugan/Skanda, given by Parvati — discriminating wisdom that pierces ignorance.

symbols.name: Tripundra
symbols.meaning: Three horizontal lines of sacred ash on the forehead — devotion to Shiva.

image.author: Vectorised by User:Sushant savla from the work by User:WarXboT
image.title: File:Rudratilaka.svg

symbols.name: Urdhva Pundra (namam)
symbols.meaning: Vertical U-shaped tilaka — the foot of Vishnu; Vaishnava devotion.

symbols.name: Kalasha / purna-kumbha
symbols.meaning: Pot of water with mango leaves and a coconut — abundance, the womb of life; the treasure vase of the Eight Auspicious Signs.

symbols.name: Shatkona
symbols.meaning: Hexagram of upward (Shiva/Purusha) and downward (Shakti/Prakriti) triangles — their union.

symbols.name: Vajra
symbols.meaning: Thunderbolt-diamond — Indra's weapon; in Vajrayana, indestructible compassion and skilful means.

symbols.name: Dharmachakra
symbols.meaning: Eight-spoked wheel of the Dharma — the Buddha's first teaching and the Noble Eightfold Path.

symbols.name: Endless knot (shrivatsa)
symbols.meaning: Interlaced knot with no beginning or end — interdependence, wisdom joined with compassion.

symbols.name: Pair of golden fish
symbols.meaning: Two fish — beings swimming free in the ocean of samsara without fear.

symbols.name: Parasol (chattra)
symbols.meaning: Royal umbrella — protection from suffering and the dignity of the Dharma.

symbols.name: Victory banner (dhvaja)
symbols.meaning: Banner of the Buddha's victory over Mara, ignorance and death.

symbols.name: Triratna
symbols.meaning: Three-pronged "three jewels" — the Buddha, the Dharma and the Sangha.

symbols.name: Bodhi leaf
symbols.meaning: Heart-shaped leaf of the fig under which the Buddha awakened — enlightenment.

symbols.name: Buddhapada (footprint)
symbols.meaning: The Buddha's footprints marked with wheels — his presence on earth.

symbols.name: Stupa
symbols.meaning: Relic mound — the Buddha's awakened mind and the elements.

symbols.name: Buddhist flag
symbols.meaning: Six vertical bands of the colours of the Buddha's aura.
symbols.note: Designed 1885; international symbol since 1950.

symbols.name: Manji
symbols.period: Buddhist imagery in East Asia from the 6th c.
symbols.meaning: The swastika 卍 in East Asian Buddhism — marks temples on Japanese maps; the Buddha's heart.

symbols.name: Ensō
symbols.meaning: Circle drawn in one stroke — enlightenment, emptiness, the moment.

symbols.name: Jain emblem
symbols.meaning: The loka (universe) outline enclosing the swastika, three dots, the siddhashila crescent and the ahimsa hand.
symbols.note: Components are ancient; the composite emblem was agreed in 1974.

symbols.name: Khanda
symbols.meaning: Double-edged sword, chakkar and two kirpans — the unity of spiritual and temporal sovereignty.
symbols.note: Its current form dates to the early 20th century.

symbols.name: Ik Onkar
symbols.meaning: ੴ "One Creator" — the opening of the Guru Granth Sahib.

symbols.name: Taijitu (yin-yang)
symbols.period: Zhou Dunyi's Taijitu (11th c.); the dotted swirl form 14th–17th c.
symbols.meaning: Interlocking black and white — yin and yang, complementary opposites each holding the seed of the other.
symbols.note: The yin-yang idea is ancient; the familiar swirl diagram is medieval (Song–Ming).

symbols.name: Bagua
symbols.period: I Ching (Zhou); arrangements drawn in Song dynasty
symbols.meaning: The eight trigrams arranged around the taijitu — every situation of heaven and earth (Earlier and Later Heaven orders).

symbols.name: Trigram Qian (Heaven)
symbols.meaning: One of the eight trigrams of the I Ching — Heaven.

symbols.name: Trigram Dui (Lake)
symbols.meaning: One of the eight trigrams of the I Ching — Lake.

symbols.name: Trigram Li (Fire)
symbols.meaning: One of the eight trigrams of the I Ching — Fire.

symbols.name: Trigram Zhen (Thunder)
symbols.meaning: One of the eight trigrams of the I Ching — Thunder.

symbols.name: Trigram Xun (Wind)
symbols.meaning: One of the eight trigrams of the I Ching — Wind.

symbols.name: Trigram Kan (Water)
symbols.meaning: One of the eight trigrams of the I Ching — Water.

symbols.name: Trigram Gen (Mountain)
symbols.meaning: One of the eight trigrams of the I Ching — Mountain.

symbols.name: Trigram Kun (Earth)
symbols.meaning: One of the eight trigrams of the I Ching — Earth.

symbols.name: Lo Shu square
symbols.period: Attested from Han texts; legend of Yu the Great
symbols.meaning: The 3×3 magic square from the turtle's back — the nine palaces, feng shui and the Later Heaven bagua.

symbols.name: Wu Xing (five phases)
symbols.meaning: Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, Water in generating and overcoming cycles.

image.title: File:Wuxing diagram mk.svg

symbols.name: Torii
symbols.period: Heian period at the latest (10th c.)
symbols.meaning: Gate marking the passage from the ordinary to the sacred at a Shinto shrine.

symbols.name: Mitsudomoe
symbols.meaning: Three swirling commas — Hachiman's crest; the triple interplay of heaven, earth and humanity.

symbols.name: Faravahar
symbols.period: Achaemenid (6th–4th c. BCE), from Assyrian winged-disc models
symbols.meaning: Winged disc with a human figure — today the best-known symbol of Zoroastrianism and of Iran.
symbols.note: What it depicted for the Achaemenids (Ahura Mazda, the fravashi, or royal khvarenah) is disputed; the fravashi reading is 20th-century.

image.author: The original uploader was Ploxhoi at English Wikipedia.
image.title: File:Faravahar.svg

symbols.name: Sacred fire / fire altar
symbols.meaning: Atar — the sacred fire, visible sign of Asha (truth) and of Ahura Mazda.

symbols.name: Mjölnir
symbols.meaning: Thor's hammer — protection, blessing (hallowing of brides and the dead); worn as a pendant in answer to the Christian cross.

image.author: Thor's_hammer,_Skåne.jpg: Chemityped by Prof. Magnus Petersen from an Electrotype in the possession of Herr Steffensen, Conservator to the Danish Museum. derivative work: Arnaud Ramey (talk)
image.title: File:Thor's hammer, Skåne.svg

symbols.name: Valknut
symbols.period: Gotland picture stones (8th c.); Oseberg ship (9th c.)
symbols.meaning: Three interlaced triangles, found with scenes of death and Odin.
symbols.note: The name "valknut" is modern; its meaning (Odin, the slain, binding) is not attested in any text.

symbols.name: Triquetra
symbols.period: Iron Age / Migration-era art; Insular gospels (8th c.)
symbols.meaning: Three interlaced vesicae — in Christian use the Trinity; in Norse art linked by some with Odin.
symbols.note: Pre-Christian meaning uncertain; Christian Trinity reading is medieval.

symbols.name: Irminsul
symbols.period: Destroyed by Charlemagne, 772 CE (Royal Frankish Annals)
symbols.meaning: Sacred pillar of the Saxons — a world-pillar holding up the sky.
symbols.note: No depiction survives. The familiar curled-top pillar is a 20th-c. reconstruction (from the Externsteine relief).

symbols.name: Vegvísir
symbols.meaning: Icelandic magical stave "so that one does not lose one's way in storms".
symbols.note: Early-modern Icelandic grimoire stave (19th-c. manuscript) — NOT Viking-age.

symbols.name: Ægishjálmur (Helm of Awe)
symbols.meaning: Eight-armed protective stave to overcome enemies and cast fear.
symbols.note: The "helm of terror" is named in Eddic poetry, but this sign is early-modern Icelandic grimoire magic, not Viking-age.

symbols.name: Triple horn of Odin
symbols.meaning: Three interlocked drinking horns — associated with the mead of poetry.
symbols.note: The link to Odin and the mead of poetry is a modern interpretation.

symbols.name: Sun cross (wheel cross)
symbols.meaning: Equal-armed cross in a circle — sun, wheel of the sun-chariot (cf. Trundholm).

symbols.name: Yggdrasil
symbols.meaning: The world-ash binding the nine worlds.
symbols.note: Common graphic renderings are modern; Eddic texts give no fixed emblem.

symbols.name: Troll cross
symbols.meaning: A bent iron ring said to ward off trolls.
symbols.note: A modern invention (1990s), marketed as folk tradition — no historical attestation.

symbols.name: Triskele (triple spiral)
symbols.period: Newgrange (c. 3200 BCE, pre-Celtic); La Tène metalwork
symbols.meaning: Triple spiral / three-armed whorl — motion, cycles; a national symbol of Ireland in modern use.

symbols.name: Celtic knot
symbols.period: Insular art (7th–9th c. — Book of Kells, Lindisfarne)
symbols.meaning: Endless interlace — eternity; decorative in Insular manuscripts.

symbols.name: Awen
symbols.meaning: Three rays from three points — poetic inspiration in modern Druidry.
symbols.note: The word awen is medieval Welsh; the three-ray symbol is Iolo Morganwg's 18th-c. invention.

symbols.name: Brigid's cross
symbols.period: Irish folk custom (Imbolc / St Brigid's day)
symbols.meaning: Four-armed rush cross hung for protection at Imbolc.
symbols.note: A pre-Christian origin is often claimed but not demonstrated.

symbols.name: Thunder mark (gromovnik)
symbols.period: Ethnographic, carved on houses (19th c. records)
symbols.meaning: Six-petalled rosette in a circle — protection against lightning, linked with Perun.
symbols.note: The Perun link is an ethnographic interpretation.

symbols.name: Kolovrat
symbols.meaning: Eight-rayed sun-wheel used by modern Slavic neopagans.
symbols.note: Modern design (1990s); also used by far-right groups — context matters.

symbols.name: Abrasax (anguipede)
symbols.meaning: Cock-headed, snake-legged god with whip and shield on amulet gems — the 365 heavens (Abrasax = 365 in Greek isopsephy).

symbols.name: Tawûsê Melek (Peacock Angel)
symbols.meaning: The Peacock Angel, chief of the seven angels to whom God entrusted the world.

symbols.name: Drabsha
symbols.meaning: Cross-shaped banner of white silk and myrtle — light and the living water.

symbols.name: Pentagram
symbols.period: Sumerian UB sign (c. 3000 BCE); Pythagorean hygieia; Agrippa (1533)
symbols.meaning: Five-pointed star — health (Pythagorean), the five wounds (medieval Christian), microcosmic man (Agrippa), spirit over the four elements (Lévi, Golden Dawn, Wicca).

symbols.name: Inverted pentagram
symbols.meaning: Two points up — Lévi's image of matter over spirit / the goat; later LaVeyan Satanism.
symbols.note: The good/evil reading of the pentagram's orientation dates from Lévi (19th c.).

symbols.name: Seal of Solomon
symbols.period: Medieval Jewish, Islamic and Christian magical texts
symbols.meaning: The signet ring of Solomon that commanded demons — drawn as a hexagram or pentagram.
symbols.note: The ring legend is late antique (Testament of Solomon); the hexagram as its image is medieval.

image.author: User Securiger on en.wikipedia, SVG version User Pitoutom on fr.wikipedia
image.title: File:Seal of Solomon (Simple Version).svg

symbols.name: Unicursal hexagram
symbols.meaning: A six-point star drawn in one continuous line — emblem of Thelema (with a five-petal rose).

symbols.name: Ouroboros
symbols.period: Enigmatic Book of the Netherworld, Tutankhamun's shrine (14th c. BCE); Chrysopoeia of Cleopatra
symbols.meaning: Serpent eating its tail — eternity, "the All is One" (hen to pan) of Greco-Egyptian alchemy.

symbols.name: Rose Cross
symbols.meaning: A rose at the centre of a cross — the unfolding of the soul on the cross of matter.

symbols.name: Eye of Providence
symbols.period: Renaissance Christian art (Pontormo, 1525); US Great Seal (1782)
symbols.meaning: An eye in a triangle with rays — God watching over humanity; the Trinity.
symbols.note: Christian in origin; Masonic use came later (1797). Not an "Illuminati" symbol historically.

symbols.name: Monas Hieroglyphica
symbols.meaning: Dee's single glyph uniting Moon, Sun, the elements and fire — the unity of the cosmos.

symbols.name: Sigillum Dei
symbols.meaning: The Seal of God — a heptagonal diagram of divine and angelic names used to call angels.

symbols.name: Sigil of Baphomet
symbols.period: Stanislas de Guaita (1897); Church of Satan (1969)
symbols.meaning: Goat's head inside an inverted pentagram with LVTHN in Hebrew letters.

symbols.name: Leviathan cross
symbols.period: Alchemical sulfur sign (17th c.); Satanic use 1969
symbols.meaning: Double cross over infinity — alchemical brimstone; later the "Satanic cross".
symbols.note: Alchemical sign is early modern; the Satanic reading dates from LaVey's Satanic Bible (1969).

symbols.name: Square and compasses
symbols.meaning: Masonic emblem — morality (square) and bounds (compasses), often with G.

symbols.name: Solomon's knot
symbols.meaning: Two interlinked loops — eternity and union across many cultures.

symbols.name: Flower of Life
symbols.period: Overlapping-circle grids from antiquity (Assyrian, Roman); name 1990s
symbols.meaning: Nineteen overlapping circles in hexagonal array.
symbols.note: The pattern is ancient; the name "Flower of Life" and its esoteric claims are 1990s New Age (Drunvalo Melchizedek). The Abydos examples are late graffiti of disputed date.

symbols.name: Seed of Life
symbols.meaning: Seven overlapping circles.

symbols.name: Metatron's Cube
symbols.meaning: Thirteen circles joined by straight lines, claimed to contain the Platonic solids.
symbols.note: Name and figure are modern New Age; not in Jewish sources.

symbols.name: Vesica piscis
symbols.meaning: Lens formed by two circles — the mandorla around Christ in majesty.

symbols.name: Enneagram
symbols.meaning: Nine-pointed figure within a circle — the law of seven and three.

symbols.name: Triple moon
symbols.meaning: Waxing, full and waning moon — the Triple Goddess of maiden, mother and crone.

symbols.name: Enochian alphabet
symbols.meaning: The "angelic" alphabet received in Dee's scrying sessions.

symbols.name: Theban alphabet
symbols.meaning: Cipher alphabet ("Honorian") used in Renaissance magic and modern Wicca.

symbols.name: Squared circle (philosophers' stone)
symbols.meaning: Circle-square-triangle-circle — the philosophers' stone uniting the elements.

symbols.name: Sun (planetary glyph)
symbols.period: Glyph forms in Byzantine manuscripts (c. 11th c.); earlier Greek papyrus abbreviations
symbols.meaning: The classical planet Sun. Gold; vitality, the self.

symbols.name: Moon (planetary glyph)
symbols.period: Glyph forms in Byzantine manuscripts (c. 11th c.); earlier Greek papyrus abbreviations
symbols.meaning: The classical planet Moon. Silver; the soul, change, the night.

symbols.name: Mercury (planetary glyph)
symbols.period: Glyph forms in Byzantine manuscripts (c. 11th c.); earlier Greek papyrus abbreviations
symbols.meaning: The classical planet Mercury. Quicksilver; communication, intellect, trade.

symbols.name: Venus (planetary glyph)
symbols.period: Glyph forms in Byzantine manuscripts (c. 11th c.); earlier Greek papyrus abbreviations
symbols.meaning: The classical planet Venus. Copper; love, beauty, harmony.

symbols.name: Mars (planetary glyph)
symbols.period: Glyph forms in Byzantine manuscripts (c. 11th c.); earlier Greek papyrus abbreviations
symbols.meaning: The classical planet Mars. Iron; will, war, drive.

symbols.name: Jupiter (planetary glyph)
symbols.period: Glyph forms in Byzantine manuscripts (c. 11th c.); earlier Greek papyrus abbreviations
symbols.meaning: The classical planet Jupiter. Tin; expansion, law, fortune.

symbols.name: Saturn (planetary glyph)
symbols.period: Glyph forms in Byzantine manuscripts (c. 11th c.); earlier Greek papyrus abbreviations
symbols.meaning: The classical planet Saturn. Lead; limitation, time, structure.

symbols.name: Uranus (planetary glyph)
symbols.period: Planet found 1781; glyph from Herschel's initial
symbols.meaning: Modern outer planet used in 19th–20th-c. astrology.

symbols.name: Neptune (planetary glyph)
symbols.meaning: Modern outer planet used in 19th–20th-c. astrology.

symbols.name: Pluto (planetary glyph)
symbols.meaning: Modern outer planet used in 19th–20th-c. astrology.

symbols.name: Aries (zodiac sign)
symbols.period: Babylonian zodiac (c. 5th c. BCE); glyphs in Byzantine manuscripts
symbols.meaning: Aries, the Ram — fire, cardinal.

symbols.name: Taurus (zodiac sign)
symbols.period: Babylonian zodiac (c. 5th c. BCE); glyphs in Byzantine manuscripts
symbols.meaning: Taurus, the Bull — earth, fixed.

symbols.name: Gemini (zodiac sign)
symbols.period: Babylonian zodiac (c. 5th c. BCE); glyphs in Byzantine manuscripts
symbols.meaning: Gemini, the Twins — air, mutable.

symbols.name: Cancer (zodiac sign)
symbols.period: Babylonian zodiac (c. 5th c. BCE); glyphs in Byzantine manuscripts
symbols.meaning: Cancer, the Crab — water, cardinal.

symbols.name: Leo (zodiac sign)
symbols.period: Babylonian zodiac (c. 5th c. BCE); glyphs in Byzantine manuscripts
symbols.meaning: Leo, the Lion — fire, fixed.

symbols.name: Virgo (zodiac sign)
symbols.period: Babylonian zodiac (c. 5th c. BCE); glyphs in Byzantine manuscripts
symbols.meaning: Virgo, the Maiden — earth, mutable.

symbols.name: Libra (zodiac sign)
symbols.period: Babylonian zodiac (c. 5th c. BCE); glyphs in Byzantine manuscripts
symbols.meaning: Libra, the Scales — air, cardinal.

symbols.name: Scorpio (zodiac sign)
symbols.period: Babylonian zodiac (c. 5th c. BCE); glyphs in Byzantine manuscripts
symbols.meaning: Scorpio, the Scorpion — water, fixed.

symbols.name: Sagittarius (zodiac sign)
symbols.period: Babylonian zodiac (c. 5th c. BCE); glyphs in Byzantine manuscripts
symbols.meaning: Sagittarius, the Archer — fire, mutable.

symbols.name: Capricorn (zodiac sign)
symbols.period: Babylonian zodiac (c. 5th c. BCE); glyphs in Byzantine manuscripts
symbols.meaning: Capricorn, the Sea-goat — earth, cardinal.

symbols.name: Aquarius (zodiac sign)
symbols.period: Babylonian zodiac (c. 5th c. BCE); glyphs in Byzantine manuscripts
symbols.meaning: Aquarius, the Water-bearer — air, fixed.

symbols.name: Pisces (zodiac sign)
symbols.period: Babylonian zodiac (c. 5th c. BCE); glyphs in Byzantine manuscripts
symbols.meaning: Pisces, the Fishes — water, mutable.

symbols.name: Air (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Hot and wet; upward triangle barred.

symbols.name: Fire (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Hot and dry; upward triangle.

symbols.name: Earth (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Cold and dry; downward triangle barred.

symbols.name: Water (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Cold and wet; downward triangle.

symbols.name: Quintessence (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: The fifth element, aether.

symbols.name: Sulfur (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Tria prima: the soul, the combustible principle (Paracelsus).

symbols.name: Mercury (principle) (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Tria prima: spirit, the fluid principle; also quicksilver.

symbols.name: Salt (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Tria prima: body, the fixed principle.

symbols.name: Gold (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: The Sun's metal; perfection.

symbols.name: Silver (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: The Moon's metal.

symbols.name: Iron (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Mars's metal.

symbols.name: Copper (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Venus's metal.

symbols.name: Tin (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Jupiter's metal.

symbols.name: Lead (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Saturn's metal; the prima materia of the Work.

symbols.name: Antimony (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: The "grey wolf" that purifies gold.

symbols.name: Arsenic (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Poison and whitener.

symbols.name: Bismuth (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Bismuth ore.

symbols.name: Vitriol (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Metal sulfates; V.I.T.R.I.O.L. — "visit the interior of the earth".

symbols.name: Sal ammoniac (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Ammonium chloride.

symbols.name: Nitre (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Saltpetre.

symbols.name: Cinnabar (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Mercury sulfide, the red stone.

symbols.name: Aqua fortis (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Nitric acid.

symbols.name: Aqua regia (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Royal water, dissolves gold.

symbols.name: Aqua vitae (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Water of life, spirit of wine.

symbols.name: Caput mortuum (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Dead head — the worthless residue.

symbols.name: Sublimation (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Process: solid to vapour and back.

symbols.name: Precipitate (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Process: deposition from solution.

symbols.name: Distill (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Process: vapour separation.

symbols.name: Dissolve (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Process: solve.

symbols.name: Purify (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Process.

symbols.name: Putrefaction (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Process: the nigredo, blackening decay.

symbols.name: Crucible (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Vessel.

symbols.name: Alembic (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Distilling vessel.

symbols.name: Retort (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Vessel.

symbols.name: Bath of Mary (balneum Mariae) (alchemical symbol)
symbols.period: Early-modern European alchemical tables (16th–18th c.); many signs older (medieval, some Greco-Egyptian)
symbols.meaning: Water bath, named for Maria the Jewess.

symbols.name: Aztec Sun Stone
symbols.meaning: Monolith carved with the four previous suns and the present age Nahui Ollin around a central face.
symbols.note: The central face — Tonatiuh or Tlaltecuhtli — is disputed.

symbols.name: Ollin (movement)
symbols.meaning: Day-sign 17, "movement/earthquake" — sign of the present Fifth Sun.

symbols.name: Feathered serpent
symbols.meaning: Quetzalcoatl / Kukulkan / Gucumatz — wind, learning, creation.

symbols.name: Hunab Ku
symbols.period: Design from Codex Magliabechiano (16th c., Aztec); labelled "Mayan" 1987
symbols.meaning: A spiral-in-square design promoted as the "Maya galactic god".
symbols.note: Hunab Ku is a colonial-era Yucatec term; the design is Aztec and its "Mayan" meaning is José Argüelles' 1987 New Age invention.

symbols.name: Chakana (Andean cross)
symbols.meaning: Stepped cross — the three worlds and four directions.
symbols.note: The stepped motif is ancient; the detailed cosmological "chakana" reading is largely 20th-c.

symbols.name: Gye Nyame
symbols.meaning: "Except God" — the supremacy of Onyame.

symbols.name: Sankofa
symbols.meaning: "Go back and fetch it" — learning from the past; the bird looking back or a heart shape.

symbols.name: Vèvè of Papa Legba
symbols.meaning: Ritual ground-drawing that calls Legba, guardian of the crossroads, to open the way.

symbols.name: Vèvè of Damballa
symbols.meaning: Twin serpents — Damballa Wedo, the primordial serpent-father.

symbols.name: Vèvè of Erzulie Freda
symbols.meaning: Pierced heart — Erzulie, lwa of love and luxury.

symbols.name: Vèvè of Baron Samedi
symbols.meaning: Cross on a tomb — the Baron, lwa of the dead.

symbols.name: Kongo cosmogram (dikenga)
symbols.meaning: Cross in a circle — the living and the dead, the sun's path through the four moments of life.
symbols.note: The detailed dikenga reading is 20th-c. scholarship (Fu-Kiau, Thompson).

symbols.name: Nine-pointed star
symbols.meaning: Nine = perfection, the numerical value of Bahá (abjad).

symbols.name: Ringstone symbol
symbols.meaning: Two stars and three bars — God, the Manifestation and the world of creation.
